# TDPdf v1.27.0.0

**A curated sync with upstream KillerPDF v1.8.0, v1.8.1 and v1.8.2. Three fixes ported, seven candidates rejected — most of them because TDPdf already had the fix, and two because ours is better.**

## The engine stays declined

Upstream's 1.8.0 headline is The KillerPDF.Engine: a bespoke .NET 10 PDF pipeline that replaces PdfSharpCore outright and takes saving, flattening, printing, page reordering and repair with it. That is a fork-defining decision, not a sync, and it stays declined. Watching it is worthwhile; adopting it is a different project.

What that leaves is the app-level work in 1.8.0 and the two maintenance releases that followed it — and most of what looked like a gap there turned out not to be one.

## A fast scroll no longer overshoots into the next page

In Single Page and Two-Page views the wheel falls through to page navigation once the scroll reaches the page boundary, so you can reach the next page without the sidebar. The catch is that a quick flick *arrives* at that boundary with notches still in flight. You meant "get to the bottom of this page"; the leftover events landed after the offset had already clamped, and the document moved on without being asked.

Two conditions now separate the two intentions. Momentum arriving within 250 ms of a real content scroll is discarded outright. After that, turning the page takes one deliberate gesture — a single geared notch, or the same distance accumulated from a precision touchpad within 650 ms — and reversing direction or pausing restarts the count, so hesitant nudges never add up across unrelated gestures.

Scrolling speed itself is unchanged. The gate also covers a page that fits the viewport entirely, where a touchpad flick used to advance one page per delta event.

## Scrolling follows your Windows mouse setting

The scroll distance was hardcoded at three times the WPF default. Whatever you had set on the Wheel tab of Mouse Properties, TDPdf ignored it — including one line at a time, and including one screen at a time, both of which people set deliberately and sometimes for accessibility.

The setting is now read per event and honoured, one screen included. Shift+wheel horizontal scrolling and the page sidebar keep the established multiplier, which is what they were tuned against.

## Ctrl+A in the Pages panel selects pages

It selected the document's text instead. The cause is worth naming: the window's shortcut handler is a *preview* handler, so it tunnels downward and claimed Ctrl+A before the page list ever saw the key.

With the Pages panel focused, Ctrl+A now selects every page, and Delete removes the selection through exactly the same confirmed, reload-backed path as the context menu's Delete Page(s).

That combination makes deleting an entire document a two-keystroke gesture, so it is now refused — a PDF cannot have zero pages, and writing one produces a file nothing will reopen. Deleting everything points you at closing the document instead.

## What was checked and deliberately not ported

Seven upstream fixes were candidates. None of them shipped, and none of them was skipped on a hunch:

- **Two-sided printing overriding the driver default** — already correct here. TDPdf has always set the one-sided case explicitly rather than leaving the print ticket untouched.
- **Multi-column text highlighting** — **ours was kept, because it is better.** Upstream now breaks ties between candidate lines using a floating-point equality test. TDPdf's caret resolution has short-circuited on true containment since the two-column selection work, and also handles right-to-left lines, which upstream's version does not.
- **Application shortcuts staying alive inside a focused text box** — **already ported, and narrowed further than upstream has now gone.** TDPdf fixed this in 1.24.1.0, once fixing the text box itself made it reachable: the gate that blocked nine commands was cut back to Undo alone, because Ctrl+Z inside a text box means "undo my typing" and every other command settles the box on its way through. Upstream's version maintains an allow-list of editing keys instead. Ours needs none, and re-entangling the active-text-box focus path to adopt theirs would buy nothing.
- **The title-bar logo crash** — cannot occur here. Upstream's declaration is a source-generated import that resolves the exact symbol name and finds no such export; TDPdf's is a classic one that probes and binds the ANSI variant.
- **Images flipping vertically when annotations are burned in**, and **text edits saving as see-through covers** — neither is our bug class. Both come from upstream writing PDF content streams directly. Our drawing library resolves page orientation itself, and our text-edit cover has always been a solid white rectangle with no blend mode to inherit.
- **The zoom shortcut label reading Ctrl+= instead of Ctrl++** — **ours was kept, because it is better.** Upstream swapped one hardcoded label for another. TDPdf works out which character is actually unshifted on your keyboard layout and labels the menu, the app-size entries and the toolbar tooltip from that one answer.
- **Microsoft Office hybrid-reference PDFs** — the fix lives entirely inside upstream's new engine's cross-reference parser. We read through PdfSharpCore and PDFium.

Unchanged from standing policy: all localization, the landing page and packaging, the split-pane viewer extraction and everything built on it (dual-pane comparison, cross-document page copying), upstream's Transform and OCR work where it now runs on their engine, the reworked installer — ours is a per-user self-installer — and the protocol handler.

Letter spacing and the measurement tool remain deferred, and are still tracked in issue #135.
